spots.name: Fuggerei
spots.summary: The Fuggerei is the world's oldest public housing complex still in use. It is a walled enclave within the city of Augsburg, Bavaria. It takes its name from the Fugger family and was founded in 1516 by Jakob Fugger the Younger as a place where the needy citizens of Augsburg could be housed.

spots.name: Augsburg Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of Augsburg is a Catholic cathedral in Augsburg, Bavaria, Germany, founded in the 11th century in Romanesque style, but with 14th-century Gothic additions. Together with the Basilica of St. Ulrich and Afra, it is one of the city's main attractions. It measures 113 x 40 m, and its towers are 62 m high.

spots.name: Eiskanal
spots.summary: The Augsburg Eiskanal is an artificial whitewater river in Augsburg, Germany, constructed as the canoe slalom venue for the 1972 Summer Olympics in nearby Munich.

spots.name: Basilica of Saints Ulrich and Afra

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica of Saints Ulrich and Afra is a Catholic parish in Augsburg in Bavaria, which originated from the Roman tomb of Saint Afra, who was martyred in 304.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Basilica of Saints Ulrich and Afra

spots.name: St. Peter am Perlach
spots.summary: St. Peter am Perlach or Perlach-Church is a romanesque Catholic church in the center of Augsburg (Bavaria). The tower of the church, the Perlachturm, is together with the Augsburg Town Hall the landmark of Augsburg.

spots.name: Rathaus
spots.summary: Augsburg Town Hall is the administrative centre of Augsburg, Bavaria, Germany, and one of the most significant secular buildings of the Renaissance style north of the Alps. It was designed and built by Elias Holl, Stadtbaumeister, in 1615–1624.

spots.name: Perlachturm

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The 70-metre-tall Perlachturm is a belltower in front of the church of St. Peter am Perlach in the central district of Augsburg, Germany. It originated as a watchtower in the 10th century. The existing Renaissance structure was built in the 1610s by Elias Holl, who also designed the neighbouring Town Hall.

spots.name: St. Anne's Church, Augsburg

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of St. Anne is a medieval Evangelical Lutheran parish church in Augsburg, Germany. Originally built in 1321, it has undergone several significant renovations since, and is notable for its elaborate interior decoration, and its role in Protestant-Catholic relations in Germany.

spots.name: Schaezlerpalais

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Schaezlerpalais is a baroque palace in Augsburg. The palace extends far back from the street, encompassing dozens of rooms, courtyards, and gardens. The gilded mirrored ballroom was built between 1765-1770 and has survived intact. It is widely regarded as the most artistically significant Rococo ballroom in Germany.

spots.name: St. Moritz
spots.summary: Parish church founded in 1019, rebuilt after fire, collapse and wartime damage. The interior people come for is new: London architect John Pawson stripped it back in 2010–13 to stone, wood and light (Cistercian-plain, not Baroque). Weekday Mass 12:15; Saturday vigil 18:00. Stay out during services if you only want the architecture.

spots.name: Augsburg Hauptbahnhof
spots.summary: Augsburg Hauptbahnhof is the main railway station in the Bavarian city of Augsburg, situated in southern Germany. It is classified by Deutsche Bahn as a category 2 station and has 12 platform tracks.

spots.name: Maximilianmuseum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Maximilian Museum is a large, public museum housed in a palatial building erected in 1546 in Augsburg, Germany. It houses a notable collection of decorative arts.

spots.name: Augsburg Railway Park

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Augsburg Railway Park is a railway museum in Augsburg on part of the former Augsburg locomotive shed owned by the Deutsche Bahn. Following reconstruction work, the park officially reopened on 13 April 2009.

spots.name: Augsburg Water Management System
spots.summary: Under the name Augsburg Water Management System, structural objects in Augsburg and the surrounding area that testify to the importance and history of Augsburg's historic water management were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site on July 6, 2019.

spots.name: Maximilianstraße
spots.summary: The Maximilianstraße is a street in the old-town area of Augsburg in Germany. It is one of the city's most historic streets and is the site of the Fuggerhäuser.

spots.name: Augsburg Zoo
spots.summary: Augsburg Zoo is a zoo located in the city of Augsburg in Bavaria, Germany, and with over 600,000 visitors annually, the zoo belongs to the 20 largest Zoos in Germany.

spots.name: Weberhaus Augsburg
spots.summary: Former weavers’ guild house. The 1389 original was the centre of Augsburg’s cloth trade until the guilds were dissolved; the painted guild parlour is now in Munich’s Bayerisches Nationalmuseum. What you see is a 1913 replacement (Otto Holzer), rebuilt after 1944 and after a 2004 fire. spots.name: Rotes Tor
spots.summary: Modern and classic fairy tales are played at the Augsburger Puppenkiste. The stars on strings are so endearing and the sets so elaborate that even non-German speakers (and non-kids) will enjoy a show. It's often sold out; make advance reservations or check with the tourist office for remaining tickets.

spots.name: Botanischer Garten Augsburg
spots.summary: The Botanischer Garten Augsburg is a municipal botanical garden located at Dr.-Ziegenspeck-Weg 10, Augsburg, Bavaria, Germany. It is open daily; an admission fee is charged.

spots.summary: Augsburg Synagogue is a synagogue on Halderstraße in Augsburg, Bavaria, Germany. It serves as the religious centre of the Israelitische Kultusgemeinde Schwaben-Augsburg, the Jewish community of Augsburg and Bavarian Swabia.

spots.summary: The Holbein-Gymnasium is a natural scientific technological and lingual Gymnasium in Augsburg. It is located in Downtown Augsburg, and partly in the Old Town of Augsburg.

spots.summary: The Catholic Holy Cross Church is a Roman Catholic parish church in the southern German city of Augsburg, Bavaria. While its history dates back to 1143 when a hospice with a chapel was constructed on the site, the present church in the Gothic style was built by Provost Vitus Fackler in 1508.

spots.name: Augsburg Protestant Cemetery
spots.summary: The Protestant cemetery in Augsburg on Haunstetter road in Hochfeld district of Augsburg was established in 1534 by the City of Augsburg. The cemetery is still in operation and used for burials. It is currently the oldest cemetery in Augsburg.

spots.summary: Augsburg Arena, currently known commercially as the WWK Arena, is a football stadium in Augsburg, Bavaria, Germany. It is used mostly for football matches and hosts the home matches of FC Augsburg.

spots.summary: The Deutsche Barockgalerie is an art gallery housed in the Schaezlerpalais in Augsburg. It was set up in 1958 and displays works from the Baroque period from the city's collection and from private lenders.

spots.summary: St. Stephen's Abbey, Augsburg is a Benedictine monastery, formerly a house of Augustinian canonesses, in Augsburg in Bavaria, Germany.

spots.name: State Textile and Industry Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The State Textile and Industry Museum, known by its acronym tim, is a museum in Augsburg a city in the south-west of Bavaria, Germany. It is situated in the Augsburger Kammgarnspinnerei, a former worsted spinning mill. The museum is an Anchor point on the European Route of Industrial Heritage.

spots.name: Brechthaus
spots.summary: The birthplace of the writer Bertolt Brecht (1898–1956).

spots.name: Bahnpark Augsburg

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Bahnpark Augsburg, a railway museum in a historic 1906 locomotive depot, showcases Europe’s railway history with locomotives like the operational 41 018, restored in its workshops. The “Rundhaus Europa” displays historic trains, complemented by a model railway and a 7¼-inch Mini-Bahn.

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed

spots.name: Water management system of Augsburg
spots.summary: In the 14th century a system of canals and watertowers were constructed in the city to provide hydraulic power among other things. This system was very innovative for its time and as such it has been inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. The World Heritage Site comprises 22 individual objects which are scattered all over town.
